title: ico penalty-schema feed payload, major 4
description: The payload half of the one feed envelope (ADR-0019) for ico's penalty-schema feed, major 4. Major 3's regimes and control_weights, plus three things eco-system ticket 79 required before any of these figures may be shown to an audience. (1) FINALITY AND SOURCING: every real example carries `source`, `status`, `final_as_of` and `litigation`, so a penalty under appeal cannot price as if it were final. Only `final` and `imposed-appeal-unchecked` price; the publisher's rule is in penalty-schema/rule.yaml. (2) FREQUENCY: every violation type publishes `frequency` -- a lo<=mode<=hi loss-event-frequency band with a `basis` naming its kind, the date it was read, its denominator and what could not be looked at. A frequency with no basis is refused by the converter (ADR-0020); the floor is 0, so a loss-free year is possible. (3) BASIS ON EVERY WEIGHT: each control weight carries the same `basis` shape, and verify-penalty-feed.sh refuses a weight without one. NOTE ON THE FILE NAME: majors 1 and 2 validate against payload.schema.v2.json and major 3 against payload.schema.json. Major 3 is published and its envelope names that bare file, so repointing it would be an unreleased edit to the newest published major -- which .github/scripts/declared-bump-gate.py refuses by design (eco-system ticket 103). From major 4 on, every major's schema is payload.schema.vN.json and the bare name stays frozen at major 3.

regimes.description: Keyed by regime name, e.g. uk-gdpr. The name an adopter declares in its obligations.

formula.description: One of pct_of_global_turnover, per_month_escalating, per_violation_tier, pct_of_relevant_revenue_plus_discretion. Each carries its own rate, cap or band fields; the converter beside this feed reads them.

items.description: One published enforcement action. `fine_gbp`/`fine_usd` is the figure the regulator IMPOSED; `notice_gbp`/`notice_usd` carries the notice figure where a later decision moved it. `status` decides whether it prices.

source.description: Where the figure comes from: the regulator's own instrument, and where a later decision moved it, what moved it and where that is recorded. REQUIRED for every example (eco-system ticket 79 review F1): before it was, an example with a `status` and no source priced -- an invented GBP 5,000,000 with status `final` moved uk-gdpr/lower-tier's mode from GBP 92,000 to GBP 2,546,000 and the feed check said PASS.

final_as_of.description: The date the figure became final, at the PRECISION the source supports: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Null for every status but `final`. Year precision is not a rounder date, it is the honest one where no source in this estate's record carries a day (review F2).

frequency.description: The publisher's own loss-event-frequency band for this violation type: how often ONE organisation in scope draws an action of this kind, per year. The converter beside this feed reads it and refuses one with no basis.

lef.description: lo <= mode <= hi, events per year. A lo of 0 makes a loss-free year possible.

basis.description: What a published number rests on. `kind` says what sort of thing it is, `statement` says it in words, `as_of` is the date it was read, and where the number is not counted, `could_not_look` says what would make it counted. A number with no basis is a missing instrument (ADR-0020), never a cheaper one.

control_weights.description: Keyed by regime name, then by violation type name. Both keys must name an entry that exists under regimes.

additionalProperties.description: Weights within one violation type sum to 1.0 (tolerance 1e-9), and each carries a `basis`.

source.description: The controls parent that defines the id, e.g. nist. Half of the (source, id) key.

id.description: A bare catalogue control id as it appears on the wire, e.g. sc-28.
